definition: <zawh> and <ding> written as one word after a verb: that can be done or finished; {gen zawhding hilo} is that cannot be told
<zawh> overcome with <gawp> marking forceful or thorough action
<zawh>, the form of <zo>, win, overcome, used before a suffix, with <huai>, worthy of: worth overcoming
<zaw>, more or rather, and the sentence ending <hi> written as one word: it is more so, or it is rather so
<zawh>, the form of <zo>, be able, overcome or finish, with the linking suffix <in>; {a teek zawhin} is after he had grown old, {hehnep zawhin om lo} is could not be comforted
<zawh>, be able or win, and <kei>, not, written as one word: after a verb, not be able to do it; alone, not win
<zawh> finish with <khit> done; {a zawhkhit ciangin} is when it has been finished
<zawh>, here finish, with <kuan>, about to, written as one word: when one is about to finish
<zawh> be able with <leh> if; {ahih zawhleh} is if it can be
<zawh> in its meaning overcome or defeat, with <leh>, if: if someone gets the better of a thing or an opponent, not if something is possible
<zawh>, be able or overcome, and <lo>, not, written as one word; after a verb: not manage to do it
<zawh> be able with <loh> not, after a verb; {sim zawhloh} is too many to count

<zawhloh>, that cannot be done, and <lungdamna>, joy or thanks: used after <gen>, say, as {gen zawhloh lungdamna}, thanks that cannot be told; a formula of public acknowledgement to donors and helpers, who stand before it with <tungah>
the fact of not being able, placed after a verb: {up zawhlohna} is inability to believe and {ngah zawhlohna} is failure to get

terms: those unable to/those that could not
definition: <zawhloh> and <te> written as one word after a verb: the ones who cannot do it, or the ones for whom it could not be done, as in {a damsak zawhlohte}, those they could not heal
the act of overcoming or of being able to do something

terms: in order to be able to/so as to manage to
definition: <zawhna>, being able or overcoming, and <dingin>, in order to: placed after a verb, so that the action can be accomplished; {neih zawhna dingin} is in order to be able to have
<zawhna>, being able or victory, with the subject marker <in>: {thuak zawhna-in} is being able to endure, as the subject of the sentence
Saying: a cat burying its dung; the book lists it among its idiomatic expressions without explaining it, apparently said of one who covers up his own wrongdoing
<zawh> overcome with <nop> easy
<zawh> finish, with <pih> do together with or for someone
<zawh> win, overcome, with <pih> do together with someone
<zawh>, overcome, with <sa> for a completed state: already conquered
<zawh>, finish, with <sa> for a completed state: already completed
<zawh>, overcome, with <sak>: cause to be overcome, or overcome on behalf of someone
<zawh>, finish or complete, with <sawm>, intend or try: set out to finish a task or reach a goal
<zawh>, form of <zo>, finish, and <siang>, clean, written as one word: finish a work entirely, so that nothing is left to do
<zawh>, the form of <zo>, win, overcome, used before a suffix, with <suah>, bring out or become: bring about or carry through what <zo> names; the page lists the form without a meaning
<zawh> finish, with plural <te>: the things he completed
<zawh>, finish, and <teh>, when, written as one word after a verb or <tua>: after doing so; {tua zawhteh} is after that
{zawhthawh thu tawh} or {thu-in} means by force
press hard on someone, force or oppress; more often found with <bawl>, as {zawhthawh bawl}
<zawhthawh>, force, and <thutawh>, by way of: placed before a verb, do it to someone by force or against that person's will
<zawhthawh>, force, with <bawl>, do, written as one word: treat someone roughly or unfairly by force, often paired with <simmawhbawl>, treat with contempt
forcing someone against his will; {zawhthawhna tawh} is by force, under compulsion
<zawhthawh> and <thu> written as one word; <zawhthawhthu tawh> is by force
<zawhthawhthu>, force, and <tawh>, with: by force, against the will of the person concerned; it stands before the verb of what is done
<zawh> win over, with <theih> can

terms: ability to accomplish/being able to do
definition: <zawhtheih> be able to overcome or accomplish, with the noun suffix <na>
getting ones way by force or by power over others; a short form of <zawhthawhthu>
<zawh>, the form of <zo>, win, overcome, used before a suffix, with <tuak>, be fitting: conquerable
<zawh>, here finish, with the plural <uh>, written as one word after a verb and before <ciangin>: after they had done it, when they had finished

terms: as much as one is able
definition: <zawh> be able with <zah> amount; {a piak zawhzah} is as much as they could give

terms: as much as one can/to the best of one's ability
definition: <zawh>, be able, with <zahzah>, as much as, written as one word after a verb: {na hih zawhzahzah} is as much as you are able to do
form of <zo> overcome followed by <zo> be able, used before <loh>, <lohna> or <nading>

terms: be able to finish/be able to complete
definition: form of <zo> finish followed by <zo> be able
a narrow path or track made by people or animals passing; also a way or channel, as in {thupha zawi}, a path of blessing
<zawi>, path, with <lui.2>, old, written as one word: the old track, and so the old way of doing things
comparative <zaw>, more than, with the adverb suffix <in>; after a descriptive word, more so, to a greater degree

terms: follow along/be in line with/be related to
definition: <zawi>, path, with <tawn>, go along: go the same way as something; mostly with the prefix <ki> written apart, {tawh ki zawitawn}, which is <kizawitawn>
form of <zaw> used after a descriptive word or verb when <leh>, <ding>, <nading> or <kei> follows; more, to a greater degree, as in {a thuk zawk} deeper
<zawk>, more, and the linking <a>, and, written as one word after a verb: do it more, and; {ih lunglut zawka} is we are more interested, and

terms: how much more/all the more/even more
definition: placed after a verb in a comparison to say that something applies to an even greater degree; after a negative verb, how much less
<zaw>, rather or more, and the particle <kha.4> written as one word after a verb: it is, or happened to be, rather so; before <ding> the writer supposes it is more likely so

<zawk> more with the noun ending <na>; after a descriptive word or verb it names the fact of being more so, as in {tam zawkna} being more numerous, {nuam zawkna} greater joy and {deih zawkna} preference
<zawk>, more, said twice after a verb of wanting such as <deih> or <ut>: whichever one prefers
a long piece of wood: a pole for carrying a load, a crossbar that holds frames together, or the bar of a city gate
the raised edge or ledge that runs round a table or an altar
a close friend, and in the old custom the sworn friend that a person or a village keeps; {zawl aw} is the way to address a friend
the person one courts: {zawl lai} is a love letter and {zawl hel} is to court
{zawl-ai}, mandrake, with <kung>, plant, and the plural <te>: mandrake plants, which Reuben found in the field
<zawl>, pole or beam, with the place marker <ah>: on the beam; in {bangtung zawlah} birds perch on the top beams of a ruined building
<zaw>, more, with <lai>, still: placed after a verb or descriptive word to say even more or still more so
placed after a descriptive word to set it against another: it is rather this than that; the book says that {zawlai} with this other meaning is written as a separate word
<zaw>, more or rather, and <leh>, if, written as one word after a verb or describing word: if it were rather so, it would be better if
<zawl>, friend or companion, with the suffix <in>: as a friend; {zawlin kiman} is be friends with, and {zawlin man} is receive as a friend, welcome
a song of love between a young man and a young woman, <la>, song, joined to the word for a sweetheart or lover; set against {Pasian la}, hymns and gospel songs

apparently <zawl>, sweetheart, with a form of the verb for visiting: the evening visit of young men to the girls; {zawllen hun} is a time of the night in the book's list, after <sawm ciahhun> and before bedtime
<zawl>, sweetheart, and <luipa>, the former one, written as one word: the man who was formerly someone's boyfriend or lover
<zawlmit>, look at someone with desire, with the linking ending <in>: looking with desire at another man's wife
<zawlmit>, look at someone with desire, with the linking ending <in>: looking with desire at another man's wife
<zawlmit>, look at someone with desire, with the noun suffix <na>: an enticing look of the eyes
<zaw> and <lo> written as one word after a verb or describing word: not more so, not rather; {thupi zawlo} is not the more important thing
a close male friend of a man; {maak thakpa' zawlpa} is the friend of the bridegroom
<zawl>, rim, with <peek>, flat piece: the flat rim or frame round the top of the table
born outside marriage, of a woman who is not the wife of the father
a child born outside marriage, not a true son or daughter

<zawl>, sworn friend, with <ta>, which names a pair or group bound to each other as in <lawmta>: friends who would give their lives and dare to die for one another; not the word for a child born outside marriage
said by a woman to her lover in {zawltai ni}, let us run off together; from <zawl>, lover, and <tai>, run
<zawl>, pole or bar, with the plural <te>: the carrying poles of the ark, the table and the altar, and the bars of a city gate
the talk of a young man and woman who are courting; {zawlthu gen} is speak of love to someone, court
Saying: a mithun fits through the gaps in <zawlthu>, the talk of lovers; in courtship a small matter easily grows into a big one
constellation named in Job together with the Bear and the Pleiades
<Zawlzawng>, Orion, with the plural <te>: the stars of Orion
without strength, said of the body and of the conscience

{zaw am}, the comparative <zaw> and the question word, written as one word, at the end of a question that asks which of two is more: {sang zawm aw} is is it higher, answered with {sang zaw e}, it is higher
Rome and the Roman empire, a Zolai form of the name; {Zawma kumpi} is the Roman emperor and {Zawma galkapte} are the Roman soldiers
<Zawma>, Roman, with <nambat>, number: a number written with the letters I, V, X, L, C, D and M

<zaw>, more, with the emphatic <mah>, written as one word, mostly in {zawmah lai} at the end of a statement: even more so, and what is more; written with a capital, {Zawmah} is a different word, the name of the Romans in writing about ancient history, as in {Zawmah galkap}, the Roman army
<zaw>, more or rather, and <mawk>, unexpectedly, written as one word after a verb or describing word: it turns out rather to be so, against what was expected
<zawm>, weak, with <cip>, completely: be worn out and without strength, from tiredness or hunger
<zawm>, weak, and <lua>, very or too, written as one word: without strength, worn out
<zawm>, weak, with the plural <te>: those who are weak; {lungsim zawmte} is the fainthearted
form of <zawng>, poor, written {zawn’} before <na>, <mahmah> and similar words; {zawn’na} is poverty
ask someone to come or to take part; after <kong> it is the usual close of a notice, {kong zawn uh hi}, we invite you, and <zawn phapha> is invite warmly; not the form of <zawng>, poor

a verb written like <zawn>, be poor, but here meaning invite or call upon, and <phapha>, well: a closing formula of notices, {kong zawn phapha uh hi}, we earnestly invite or urge you, after a clause that says what the readers are asked to do
having little money or property; also used as a verb, be poor or become poor
a monkey, named in sayings together with <ngau>, the langur

Saying: the monkey does not see its own rump and points out the rump of its friends, where the book prints <kheng> or <khawn>; said of those who do not see their own faults and keep telling only those of their friends
Saying: what the monkey ate, the langur pays for; one person suffers for the bad conduct of another
<zawng>, poor, with the linking ending <in>: being or becoming poor, and so something else follows
the animal name <zawng>, monkey, with the doer marker <in>: the monkey as the one that does something, as in {zawngin an ane}, the monkey eats the crop; not the word for poor
without strength or power; also used as a verb, grow weak or be worn out
<zawngkhal> weak and helpless, with the ending <in>
weakness or sickness of the body; of crops, {ankung zawngkhalna} is blight or mildew
the state of being poor and without power
<zawngkhal>, weak, with the causative <sak>: make weak or powerless
<zawngkhal>, weak or feeble, with the plural suffix <te>
carry a person or a body out of a place, several people lifting together, as on a stretcher; a verb of carrying between two or more people, with <khia>, out; not <zawng>, poor
a kind of monkey or ape; compare <zawngkuhpi>, a large ape
a large ape; in the articles an orangutan, and a Zolai dictionary gives it for the large apes as a kind
<zawng>, poor, with <lua>, too or very
animal brought by the ships of Tarshish together with ivory and peacocks
<zawng>, poor, with <pa>, which marks a man: a poor man; often {mi zawngpa} or {sanggam zawngpa}, a poor brother
<zawng>, poor, with <pen>, most: poorest
<zawng>, poor, with <pen>, most, and the plural <te>: those who are the poorest
large kind of monkey, brought by the ships of Tarshish together with <zawngmaw>
<zawng>, poor, with the causative <sak>: make someone poor, take away what he has
<zawngsak>, make poor, with the linking suffix <in>: making poor, and then another action follows
a tree, Parkia, grown in the Zomi hills for its long edible pods, and the pods themselves
<zawng>, here monkey and not the word for poor, and <tawh>, with, written as one word: with monkeys, or with <kibang>, like a monkey
<zawng>, poor, with the plural <te>: poor people, usually as {mi zawngte} or {a zawngte}
the animal monkey, as in <zawngmaw>, with the plural <te>: monkeys; the sentence speaks of animals of the forest, not of people in need
<zawng>, poor, with <zaw>, more, written as one word: poorer; <sang> marks what it is compared with
<zawn>, take someone along as a companion, with the linking suffix <in>
a form of <zawng>, poor, with <lawh>, as a result: become poor through something that happens, lose one's wealth by it; often with <ki>
<zawn>, be poor, with the noun suffix <na>: the state of being poor
<zawnna> poverty, with the plural <te>
the book gives it, together with <dualdap>, as the opposite of <hanciam>, strive: apparently making no effort, slack
<zawn>, be poor, and <tat>, act, written as one word: do a thing in a poor way because one is poor, set against <lianzat>

terms: the greater one/one who is more
definition: <zaw> more, with <pa> for a man, placed after a descriptive word: {a lian zawpa} is the one who is greater
<zaw>, more, and <pah>, at once, written as one word after a describing word or verb: it becomes more so straight away
<zaw> more, with the intensifier <pek>, placed after a descriptive word: {manpha zawpek} is worth far more
<zaw>, more, and the topic marker <pen> written as one word, after a describing word: the one that is more so, as in {athasang zawpen}, the taller one
<zaw>, more, and <pian>, likeness, written as one word and placed after a verb or describing word before <hi>: it is rather so, it seems or tends to be so
<zaw>, weak, with the causative <sak>: make weak or powerless; {khut zawsak} is let the hands drop, give up
placed after a descriptive word, apparently <zaw> more with a further element: {a hoih zawsang om tuan lo}, nothing any better comes of it
<zaw>, more, with the further of <semsem>, not the verb work; placed after a describing word
placed after a verb to mark what is done or happens in place of what was expected or wanted
<zawsop> instead, with <in> linking it to what follows
feel about with the hands as a blind person does or as in the dark; also search through things by hand
<zaw>, more, and the particle <ta> written as one word, after a verb or describing word: it has now become more so
another form of the Bible name Joseph, used for the son of Jacob and for Joseph of Arimathea

terms: rather I wonder/would it be better
definition: <zaw>, more or rather, and the wondering question word <tam> written as one word at the end of a question: which rather, I wonder, as in {kua nagum zawtam}, whom would you rather defend; not <tam>, many
<zaw>, more, with the plural <te>, placed after a descriptive word or verb: those who are more so, as {a vanglian zawte}, the stronger ones, and {a it zawte}, those who love more
<zaw>, weak, with the plural <te>; {khe zawte} is those whose feet are weak, the lame
<zaw> more, with <tham>, placed after a verb in a how much more comparison
<zawtham> and <pah> written as one word after a describing word: much more so, all the more
<zaw>, more, and <thei>, can, written as one word after a verb: can do it more, is more likely to
feel about with the hands again and again, as a blind person searching for a door
<zaw>, more, said twice: whichever is the more so; <khat zawzaw> is either one, one or the other
<zaw>, more, and <zek>, a little, written as one word after a verb or describing word: rather, somewhat more than expected
placed after a verb and before <zong>, even if, to strengthen the supposition: {hong ding zawzen zongun}, even if they were actually to stand
placed after a verb in a plain statement or question, often before <hi>, to stress that something really is so or went that far; without <zong> there is no supposition
placed after a verb phrase: to such a degree that, not even; from <zaw> more and <zen> emphatic with <in>
<za>, hundred, said twice: by hundreds, in groups of a hundred each; often with <tultul>, by thousands
<za>, hear, said twice to show hearing that is repeated or goes on and on
son of Jonathan, a descendant of Jerahmeel of the tribe of Judah
<za>, hear, with <zo>, which marks the action as done or achieved: have heard
a body of Zomi Baptist churches with its head office in Myanmar, written with its initials; also in the names of its member churches abroad
English abbreviation of a Zomi church body; the articles write it out both as Zomi Christian Alliance and as Zomi Christian Assembly
abbreviation of Zomi Congress for Democracy, a Zomi political party in Myanmar
abbreviation of Zomi Community Development Center, a building project of the Zomi community
abbreviated name of the Zomi Christian Literature Society, a publisher and bookshop of Zolai books with its office in Kalaymyo
Midianite leader captured and killed in the time of Gideon, together with Oreb
put a person to the test, or tempt someone to do wrong; always written with a hyphen
<ze-et>, test or tempt, with the noun suffix <na>: a temptation, a trial or a testing
<ze-et>, test or tempt, with the noun suffix <na> and the plural suffix <te>
place on the northern border of the promised land, also spelled <Zedad>
second word of the name New Zealand, a country in the Pacific; written {New Zealand gam}
name given to Simon, one of the twelve apostles
chief god of the Greeks; the people of Lystra called Barnabas by this name
king of Midian defeated by Gideon, named together with Zalmunna
name of several men, among them two Benjamites and a priest of the family of Immer in the time of Ezra
king of Midian captured and killed by Gideon, together with Zalmunna
fisherman of Galilee, father of the apostles James and John
son of Seir the Horite and father of Aiah and Anah
mother of King Jehoiakim of Judah, daughter of Pedaiah of Rumah
descendant of Nebo who had married a foreign wife in the time of Ezra
first part of {Zeboi-im}, Zeboyim, one of the cities of the plain named with Sodom, Gomorrah and Admah
one of the cities of the plain; its king Shemeber fought beside the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah
one of the cities of the plain, named with Sodom, Gomorrah and Admah on the border of Canaan
town of Benjamin settled after the exile; also a valley in Benjamin facing the wilderness
governor of the city of Shechem under Abimelek, who drove Gaal out of the city
sixth son of Jacob and Leah, ancestor of the tribe of Zebulun; also the tribe and its territory
the people of the tribe of Zebulun
place on the northern border of the promised land
name of several men, among them the last king of Judah and a false prophet in the time of Ahab
Midianite leader killed at the winepress of Zeeb in the time of Gideon, together with Oreb
handle money, time or goods with care so that they are well used; {sum zeek} is manage money
the managing of property or money for another
<zeek> manage or have charge of, with the plural <te> and <in>, as: as those who have charge of something
<zeek>, manage, and <zia>, way, written as one word: how time, money or goods are managed and used with care
of news or a scent, reach every part of a place; written with a long vowel, the same word as <zel>
placed after a verb for an action done time after time; written with a long vowel, the same word as <zel>
<zeel> often, with the linking suffix <in>
<zeel> spread through, with causative <sak>: cause news to spread through a place

terms: all over the place/here and there/in disorder
definition: placed after a verb: the action goes on everywhere and without order, as talk that goes round or people who stay scattered; probably the same word as <zelzul>
make beautiful: used of a building, a tomb or the hair, and of dressing a person in fine clothes
<zeem> adorn, with the linking suffix <in>; of the eyes, to put on eye paint
<zeem> adorn, with <sak>: dress another person in fine clothes
thin and slender, said of the body or a part of it
name of several men, among them a priest in the time of Jeremiah and the prophet Zephaniah
<Zefath>, Zephath, with the place marker <ah>: in Zephath, a Canaanite city that was destroyed and renamed Hormah
valley near Mareshah in Judah where King Asa drew up his army for battle
man of the tribe of Manasseh, son of Hepher, who had five daughters and no sons
first part of Zaphenath-Paneah, the name Pharaoh gave to Joseph
the Egyptian name Pharaoh gave to Joseph
son of Eliphaz and grandson of Esau, called Zepho in Genesis
son of Eliphaz and grandson of Esau, a chief of Edom
son of Gad, ancestor of the Zephonite clan
ritually defiled or unclean; in 1 Corinthians 8:7 said of people of weak conscience who think of themselves as defiled after eating food offered to idols
a thing that defiles what is holy; {a lipkhaphuai zehphitna} is the abomination that causes desolation spoken of by Daniel
clean according to the ritual law and so fit to take part in worship; said of priests and Levites who had purified themselves

a time in which people keep away from certain things by rule: the Lent of the Catholic church and of Buddhist monks, a traditional time of taboo in a village, and the quarantine kept against a disease
Jesus of Nazareth, the Christ; a Tedim spelling of the name, also written <Jesuh>
<Zeisu>, Jesus, written in capital letters in the notice placed above him on the cross
<Zeisu>, Jesus, and <Khazih>, Christ: the name and title together, as used by the churches that write the name in this spelling; often after <Topa>, Lord

expressive word placed after a verb, describing many things lying, falling, hanging or shining spread out over a wide area: {paak zeizai} is strewn everywhere, {tuk zeizai} is fall dead all over a field
<zeizai>, spread all over, with the noun suffix <na>: a place where many things hang or lie all about; in Song of Songs 4:4 the tower on which a thousand shields hang
placed after a word of time, amount or distance: a little, a short while; {a den zek ciangin} is a little later, {kumkhat val zek} is a little over a year
the verb <zeek> written with a short vowel: spend or use money and goods, often paired with <zat> and with <kep>, keep; {sum zek} is spending money
be late or slow in doing something, put it off; mostly with a negative, {zekai lo}, without delay
<zekai>, be late, with the causative <sak>: make someone late, hold someone back
<zek>, spend or use, and <dan>, way, written as one word: how money or a thing is spent, used or managed
<zek>, spend or use, and <ding> written as one word: will be spent, is to be used
name of many men, among them the prophet Zechariah son of Berekiah and the priest who was the father of John the Baptist
son of Jeiel of Gibeon, of the tribe of Benjamin
<zek>, spend, and <khia>, out, written as one word: lay out money for a purpose
<zekna> management, handling of what is entrusted, with <ah> in
cause to manage, with causative <sak>
be skilful, <siam>, in spending or laying out money and goods; paired with <zangsiam>, use skilfully
expressive word placed after a verb or a colour word: spread or spattered all about, as red spit of betel or things lying around; {san zekzak} is bright red
placed after a verb or describing word: it is so in some cases or at some times, not throughout; {om zekzek} is occur now and then
placed after a verb for an action done time after time or by custom
of fame, news or praise: spread and reach throughout a land
town of Benjamin where Saul and Jonathan were buried in the tomb of Kish
<zel>, spread, with <dikdek>, thoroughly, and <zo>, written as one word: of news, spread right through a land or the whole world
<zel>, repeatedly or in turn, with <ding>, will, written as one word after a verb: will do or be so again and again, or in turn
an Ammonite, one of the mighty warriors of David
form of <zel> spread over, used before <bangin>
<zel> and <hi> written as one word at the end of a statement: the action is done regularly or again and again
<zel>, spread over, with the marker <in>: spreading through a whole area
<zel>, repeatedly, with the linking marker <in> after a verb
<zel>, repeatedly, and <mawk> written as one word after a verb: it keeps happening, said with regret or surprise

<zel>, repeatedly, with the noun suffix {-na}, placed after a verb: the doing of it again and again, or the place where it is usually done; {nong phawk zelna uh} is your remembering me time after time
son of Hepher of the tribe of Manasseh, who had no sons and whose five daughters received his inheritance
<zel> spread through, with <pak> quickly, of news
<zel>, habitually, with the plural <te> written as one word after a verb: those who do it often or regularly
place on the border of Benjamin near the tomb of Rachel
descriptive word placed after a word of colour, quality or motion, giving a picture of something that shines, is smooth or moves swiftly: {kang zelzal} is gleaming white, {hoih zelzal} fine and smart
placed after a verb to show that the action happens over and over
<zelzel>, repeatedly, and <ding>, will, written as one word after a verb: will or should go on doing it time after time
<zelzel>, repeatedly, with the ending <in>, placed after a verb
<zelzel> and <khat> written as one word after a verb: one who does it again and again, a person or thing that habitually does so
<zelzel>, again and again, with the noun suffix <na>: the fact that something is done or happens many times; {na nat mun zelzelna} is your frequent illnesses
<zelzel> again and again, with the plural <te>, after a verb: {a khialthei zelzelte}, those who err again and again
in disorder, confused; in 1 Corinthians 14 said of what God did not call his people to be, set against {hoihtak nuamtakin}, in a good and peaceful way
make something beautiful by adding ornament, as overlaying an idol with silver and gold, decorating a tomb or working cloth with coloured thread
town of Benjamin near Bethel; also a mountain in the hill country of Ephraim
a Canaanite people descended from Canaan son of Ham
<zem>, decorate or adorn, with the linking marker <in>; of a person, dressing in fine clothes, and of the eyes, putting on paint
son of Beker and grandson of Benjamin
beautifully adorned, said on the page of the peacock; the first part is <zem>, decorate
<zem>, decorate, with the causative <sak>: dress another person in fine clothes

son of Bilhan, a descendant of Benjamin
one of the seven eunuchs who served King Xerxes

chief god of the Greeks; the people of Lystra called Barnabas by this name
expressive word placed after a descriptive word to strengthen it; {mam zeza} is quite straight, {san zeza} is bright red

the way something is done, placed after a verb or verbal noun as in {hih zia}, way of doing
a man of the tribe of Gad, head of a family

<zia>, way, and <ding>, to be, written as one word after a verb: the way something is to be done, how to do it; common in headings
used doubled, {ziah ziah}, after a verb: steadily, in a continuous flow, one after another without holding back; the same as <ziahziah> written as two words
placed after a verb for something that pours down, blazes or shoots up in a great mass, as falling earth, flames or lava; compare <ziahziah>
placed after a verb of giving or spending: without holding back
placed after a verb of action, as <kap ziahziah>, keep firing, and {bomb khiat ziahziah}, drop bomb after bomb: the action goes on in quick succession or in great numbers, with no thought of giving
<ziahziah>, one after another, and <detna> written as one word after a verb, before the noun of a place: where cars or people constantly pass in great numbers, busy
<ziahziah> and <in> written as one word after a verb: doing it fast and without stopping, as tears flowing or keys being pressed
<ziahziah>, freely and in great numbers, with the noun suffix <na>, placed after a verb: the doing of it by many or without stop, and before <mun> or a place word the place where this goes on
<ziahziah> after a verb with <ta>, already, written as one word: the action is already going on freely and at full strength, as a fire already blazing or a work already well under way
<ziahziah>, freely or one after another, with the plural <te>, after a verb with <a>: those who do it freely, as {a hawmkhia ziahziahte}, those who give out freely
placed after a verb for things scattered or pouring out all over, as luggage thrown about or sweat running

expressive word placed after a verb or describing word: in a bright, showy or fluttering mass, said of flowers covering a car and of things flying through the air; dictionaries give resplendent, splendid

<ziakai>, be late, and <cip>, completely, written as one word: of trains and aircraft, be held up and unable to leave
<ziakai>, be late, and <ding>, will, written as one word: there will be a delay, often after the length of time

<ziakai>, be late, with the noun suffix {-na}: a delay, or something that holds back
<ziakai>, be late, with the causative <sak>: cause a flight, a train or a journey to be late; also used for be delayed

terms: can take/may take as long as

<zial> and <khat> written as one word, after <zaa>, tobacco: one cigarette

<ziau> and <mawk> written as one word, placed after a verb: the thing is done at once and without more ado, often with a note of surprise at how lightly it was done
<ziau> with the noun suffix <na>, after a verb: the act of simply or readily doing it, as in {up ziauna}, mere believing, and {sim ziauna}, just reading

placed after a verb: do something lightly and readily, as changing the mind again and again or bringing out whatever one pleases; exact force not confirmed

<zumkong>, the door of an office, and <mangkong>, the door of an official, said as a pair: the offices and courts of the government, the authorities before whom a dispute or a case is brought; often before a verb of reaching or reporting, as {zumkong mangkong kitun}, go to court against each other

<zum>, office, with <lam>, side: the office or the authorities as the party that acts; {zumlam panin} is from the authorities
<zum>, be ashamed, with the noun suffix <na>: shame or disgrace; {zumna thuak} is be put to shame
<zumna>, shame, written with a capital at the start of a line or sentence; {zumna mel thei lo} is shameless
<zumna>, shame, and <mel>, appearance, written as one word: any look or sense of shame, mostly with a negative, without shame
<zum>, office, with <nasem>, worker: a person who works in an office
<zum> in the sense office with <nuai> written as one word: at the lower side of an office or station, as in {Palik zumnuai}, below the police station

terms: go to the office/go to work
definition: <zum>, office, and <pai>, go, written as one word: go to the office, attend work at an office
<zum>, office, and <pan>, from, written as one word, after the name of the office: from that office
<zum>, office, with the augmentative <pi>: the office or main office of a government body, an organisation or a church; {thukhenna zumpi} is a court
<zum>, be ashamed, with <pih>: feel shame because of someone or something, be ashamed of one's people, parents or conduct
<zumpi>, office, and <sung>, inside, written as one word: the inside of an office, in the office
<zumpi>, office, with the plural <te>: offices, and the people of an office
<zumpi> and <ten> written as one word: the office or offices as the ones who say or announce something
<zum>, be ashamed, with the causative <sak>: make someone ashamed
a day name taken from Meitei, Manipuri, given as Friday in the book's table of the days of the week; the Meitei calendar itself has Yumsakeisa, Wednesday, so the day is to be confirmed
<zum>, office or court, and <sung>, inside, written as one word: the office as a place of work, in the office
<zum>, office or court, with the plural <te>: offices; {kumpi zumte} are government offices and {thukhen zumte} are the courts of law
the end of the working day at the office, when people go home; the counterpart of <zumkah>, go to work, and formed like <sangtuah>, school is out; {zumtuah hun} is the evening rush hour

terms: come off work/leave the office/finish work
definition: <zum>, office, with <tuak>: come away from the office at the end of the working day, paired with <zumkah>, go to work; also the time of leaving work
<zum>, office, with <vai>, affair: business that has to be done at or with an office or the authorities
the liquid waste of the body; in the verses paired with <ek>, excrement
of fruit on the tree or vine, often after <min> ripe: {a min a zun}, {min zun mahmah}, very ripe; used where the English has first ripe or early fruit; exact sense not certain
look after and build up a land or a people so that it thrives, often paired with <puah>, repair; a verb, not the noun urine
<zun>, here the noun urine, <leh>, and, <ek>, excrement: the fixed pair for the waste of the body; {zun leh ek pai} is to relieve oneself
<zun>, urine, with <buk>, here a hut or shelter: a place for passing urine; often named together with <ekbuk>
drink liquor, from <zu>, fermented drink, and <ne>, consume; mostly in the pair {anne zune}, eat and drink
form of <zune>, drink liquor, used before another word: {zunek a hatte} is those strong at drinking, {zunek ding} is what is to be drunk
<zunek>, drink liquor, with the noun suffix <na>: the drinking of wine or other alcoholic drink, also heavy drinking
the part of a plant or tree that grows in the ground; {zung kha} means take root
<zung>, root, written with a capital in the title {David’ Zung}, the Root of David, and at the start of a quotation
<zung>, root, with <bawh>, pull up: tear a plant out with its roots
<zungbawh>, uproot, with the linking ending <in>: uprooting and then
a ring worn on the finger; {min gelhna zungbuh} or {min thuhna zungbuh} is a signet ring used for sealing

terms: as a ring/as a signet ring
definition: <zungbuh> ring with the marker <in>, here as or like: make someone as a signet ring
plural of <zungbuh> finger ring; {min gelhna zungbuhte} are signet rings
a ring worn on the finger, in the articles a wedding or engagement ring; another form of <zungbuh>
the finger used for pointing, named with <kawk>, point; the page lists the word without a meaning
<zung>, root, with <kha>: strike root, become firmly fixed; also written apart as {zung kha}
apparently <zung>, root, with <kha>, bitter: in Hebrews 12.15 {zungkha a nei singkung} is a plant with a bitter root that grows up and harms many, where the other text has {a kha kung a zung}
<zung>, root, and <kip>, be firm, written as one word: of a tree, have roots that hold fast; of love or belief, be deeply rooted
pull out by the roots; of people, remove them completely from their land
<zung>, root, with <pan>, from, written as one word
<zung>, root, with <pi>, great: the main root that keeps the branches alive
plural of <zung>: the roots of a tree or plant
<zung>, root, with <thuk>, deep, used with <kha>: strike deep roots, be firmly rooted
a cut of a slaughtered animal named in the customary division of meat, mostly written <azungzui>; the page gives it as the same cut as <anaakbul>, and does not say which part of the body it is
intensifier placed after a describing word: {nuam zungzung} very pleasant, {lim zungzung} very tasty, {khum zungzung} very sweet, {gim zungzung} very tiring

a named cut of a slaughtered animal, the share of the <zinkhak> and of the lesser kin and neighbours when the meat is shared out at the sending off of a bride; one side of it, {a zungzuui langkhat}, goes with the party that takes the bride; which part of the animal it is, is not stated on the page
<zun>, tend, and <in> written as one word, after <puah>, repair: tending and building up; in one article it stands for <zuanin>, heading for
<zun>, urine, with <khum>, sweet: diabetes, the disease of too much sugar in the blood, also {zunkhum natna}
the passage by which urine leaves the body, from <zun>, urine, and <lampi>, way
pass <zun>, urine, onto a thing or a place, squirt urine at it
<zun>, urine, with <suak>, here come out: pass urine, also the need to do so
<zunsuak> and <pahpah> written as one word: need to pass urine again and again
<zun>, urine, with <tha>, here let out: pass urine
<zun>, urine, and a verb for passing it out of the body, also written {zun a thak}; as a noun, urination
the passing of <zun>, urine, and the place for it; {zunthakna lampi} is the urinary tract and {pasal zunthakna} the men's toilet
<zu>, rice beer, with <pan>, here apparently begin: heading of the rules that say which holder of a household position starts on whose rice beer; the exact sense of <pan> here is not settled
name of a share of the meat at a funeral, received by the Thalloh and by the meat stewards of the wife's kin; it ends in <sa>, meat, and the page does not explain the name
heavily drunk with <zu>, alcoholic drink; also a person in that state
<zu>, beer, with <phih>, spit: the beer that the priest sprays from his mouth as an offering at the household sacrifice
found only in {zuphung pa}, the man in charge of a wedding feast, master of the banquet; <zu> is wine
name of two men: a Midianite chief, father of Kozbi, killed by the Israelites, and a Benjamite of Gibeon, a brother of Kish
city in Switzerland
son of Abihail, leader of the Merarite clans of the Levites
father of Shelumiel, the leader of the tribe of Simeon in the wilderness
small gnawing animal, a rat or mouse, counted among the unclean animals
<zusa>, rat, and <vasa>, bird, used as a pair and joined with a hyphen: rats and birds, the small creatures that eat the crops
<zu>, liquor, with <sai.3>, shop: a place where alcoholic drink is sold and drunk
<zu>, fall, with the causative <sak>: make rain, hail or food fall from the sky
cause something to fall or come down from above, said of God sending rain, fire or manna
<zusak>, cause to fall or rain, with the linking ending <in>: sending down, and so
<zusa>, mouse or rat, with the plural <te>
<zu>, fall, said of rain, with <suk>, downward: pour down
coat or smear a surface with pitch, plaster or the like
cover a surface with a layer of gold or bronze
pass the hand or a cloth over a surface, to rub the skin gently or to wipe something off, with nothing left on it as a coat; {puansiang tawh zut} is wipe with a clean cloth
given by the book in brackets as another word for <zukhaihsa>, the beer served in welcome; <zu>, beer, with a second part that the book does not explain
<zu> wine or fermented drink with the plural <te>; {leenggah zute} is wine of grapes
pledge given to seal a promise of marriage, literally a flask of <zu>, rice beer; {zuthawl piaksa} means pledged to be married, betrothed
<zu>, liquor, with <thawl>, bottle: an actual bottle of beer, whisky or other liquor, full or empty, with no thought of the marriage pledge
<zut>, overlay or smear, with the linking ending {-in}: coat with gold, rub with oil, paint the eyes
<zut>, smear or coat, with <kha>, happen to, written as one word: of hair, have put colour on it
connective form of <zutkhia>, from <zut> rub or strip with <khia> out: stripping fruit off a plant and then
<zut>, smear, plaster or overlay, with the noun suffix <na>; the material for plastering a wall, or the overlaying of a surface
<zut>, rub or wipe, with the causing <sak>, written as one word: rub or wipe a part of another person
apparently <zut> rub with <siang> clean: rubbed bright, said of bronze
<zut>, rub or draw across, with <tan>, sever, written as one word: cut through by drawing something such as a wire across
strong alcoholic drink, <zu>, that is made and sold; in the articles a spirit that poisoned those who drank it
<zut> said twice: rub, stroke or smear again and again, as stroking a new car, rubbing oil on something, or swiping on a phone
go along with what others do or with an earlier pattern; close in meaning to <zui>
look after something and keep it in good order, often paired with <puah>, repair
<zuun>, tend or put in order, with the linking <in>, written as one word: tending and, followed by another verb
<zuun>, tend and put in order, with the noun ending {-na}; {minam zuunna} is the tending and building up of a people
<zuun>, tend or put in order, with <siam>, skilled: know how to handle or arrange something well
<zu>, of rain, fall, and <ziahziah>, heavily and without stopping, written as one word; used after <guah>, rain
people living in Ham, east of the Jordan, who were defeated by Kedorlaomer
<zu>, alcoholic drink, and <zong>, also, written as one word
a mountain near Hpa-an in Karen State, Myanmar
abbreviation of Zomi Youth Association, a youth organisation of the Zomi with branches in Myanmar, India and other countries
<ZYA>, the Zomi Youth Association, with the plural <te>: the members or branches of the association
a Zomi village in the Champhai district of Mizoram, India
<kong> and <suaksak> written as one word: we bring it out for you, said by those who publish a piece of news or writing
the examination at the end of high school and the pass in it
<gamuk> with the plural ending <te>: those who govern a country, its government

terms: according to/in line with/at the level of
definition: in the writing of a few authors, after a noun and followed by {-in} or {-a}: in keeping with or on the scale of what is named, as {hunlem zil-in}, as time allows, and {minam zil-a}, at the level of the people; also a word of traditional songs, not described here
a village in Tedim township, Chin State; written after the name of a person it tells the home village
an island territory in the North Atlantic, in the articles mostly in the name Bermuda Triangle
the great traditional feast of the Zomi, given by a husband and wife over several days with the killing of mithun and the singing of its own songs
the level or standing that a person, a people or a country has reached, glossed by its writers with English level
the Kurds, a people of Iraq, Syria, Turkey and Iran, and what belongs to them
the life of people together in family, neighbourhood and community; used by some writers for English social, as {sahkhua thutanna}, social justice
<va> and <sak> written as one word: go and sing, in {la vasak pih}, go and sing songs together with others
the Chinese martial art
the traditional woven skirt of Zomi women, from <Zo> and <niik>, skirt; named together with <Zopuan>
plural of <Laimi>: the Lai people of the Hakha and Falam area of Chin State
<hibang> and the linking <a> written as one word: like this, in this way, of this kind
a word of songs and poetry for a pleasant, fortunate and successful life, said of a life, a time or a land; {nunnuam gam} is a land of happy life
the giving of a name, from <vawh>, name; {min vawhna} is the naming of a person, a place or a thing
the sowing of seed, or the place where seed is sown, from <vawh>, sow; {khaici vawhna} is the sowing of seed
the first word of the name Boko Haram, an armed Islamist group of Nigeria; the full name is written {Boko Haram}
the traditional bead necklace of the Zomi, from <Zo> and <khi>, necklace; named together with <Zopuan> and <Zodial>
<om> and <laai> written as one word: still be there, there still is, still remain
a mountain by Tungzang village in the Tedim area, called {Teute vum}, which tradition says is guarded by spirits
a kind of traditional Zomi woven cloth, named together with <Puandum>, <Puanlaisan> and <Khephiau>; which garment it is exactly is not confirmed
a town in West Bengal, India, known for Serampore College and its theological degrees
a village in Champhai District in the east of Mizoram, India
the second word of the name Boko Haram, an armed Islamist group of Nigeria; the full name is written {Boko Haram}
<kasa> and <hi> written as one word at the end of a sentence: I think so, I find it so
one who holds to an agreement, from <thukhun> and <pom>; in {Genvai Thukhunpom} a subscribing member of the Zomi funeral aid fund in the USA
<zop>, continue, said twice as one word: go on continuing; {zopzop lai ding} at the end of an article is to be continued
the way a people or group is governed and manages its own affairs, from <kivaihawm>; {ei leh ei kivaihawmna} is self-determination
<ahih> and <ziak> written as one word, mostly followed by <in>: because it is so, because of being
short name of Sawbuayeshin, a Zomi village and ward in the <Kalay> area of Myanmar
one who shares the same blood, from <sisan>, blood, and <pih>, fellow: a relative by blood, and more widely a person of the same people
<Zo> and <tate>, children, written as one word: the descendants of Zo, a name the Zomi use for themselves as one people
<sem> and the linking <a> written as one word: working as, having worked, and then the sentence goes on
the Shia branch of Islam and its followers, named beside the Sunni; {Shia Muslim} is a Shia Muslim
closes a short question that asks in turn about the thing just named: and what about it, and how about that one
<ih> and <ko> written as one word, in {lungdam ihko hi}: we give thanks
<i> and <mipihte> written as one word: our fellow people, those of our own kind
<i> and <nuntaakna> written as one word: our life
taken in from outside and made one's own: {toptawm nau} is an adopted child, and {toptawm kammal} a word borrowed from another language, as in {Kawlpau toptawm}, borrowed from Burmese
the community that people live in together; before a noun it means social, as in {khotang nuntakna}, social life, and {khotang kipawlna}, a civil society organisation
the language of Tedim and its region, <Tedim> with <pau>, language; also used for the Zomi language as a whole
word of songs and elevated prose for strength of body or of heart, explained in a song glossary as <thatang>

terms: how to know/how can one know
definition: <bangcih> and <theih> written as one word, before <ding>: how one can know
<ipiak> and <ngamding> written as one word: that we dare to give, we should be ready to give
<la>, song, with <sin>, learn: the practising of songs by a choir or group, and to practise them
form of <khangkhia>, grow up, used before <ding>, <na> and in dependent clauses; {khankhiat na mun} is the place where one grew up
the traditional head covering of Zomi women, pointed and hanging down at the back, from <Zo> and <lukhu>, head covering
word of songs used with <dam>: <tangbang dam> is be well, be in good health, explained in a song glossary as <cidam>
word of songs for someone else, a person who is not one's own; {singdang ang} is the arms of another and {singdang gamlei} a foreign land
<hong> and <hi> written as one word: comes to be, becomes, turns out to be
traditional Zomi dance at feasts, in which men and women link arms in a line and step together to the beat of the drum while singing; also to dance it
the traditional woven shoulder bag of the Zomi, from <Zo> and <thungkuah>, shoulder bag
word of songs and elevated prose used with <leng>: {laitual leng} is live and move about in a place, {laitual lengkhawm} is live together, and {laitual lenna} is the place where people live
<kitukalh>, be at odds, with the noun suffix {-na}: a clash of views, wishes or groups
<sik>, pay for, and <lo>, not, written as one word: does not bear the cost, said of what an insurance or a company does not pay
how a person sees and takes a matter, from {muh leh saanna}, seeing and taking; {mimal muhlehsaanna} is a personal opinion
sentence-final particle of speech that presses a statement on the hearer as plain or already known: you see, after all, I tell you; compare <ve>
think about something, used mostly in writing of the Paite and related dialects where Tedim writing has <ngaihsun>
<ka>, my, and <hun>, time, written as one word: my time, the time I have
the land of old legend said to lie sunk under the ocean; also the name of a space shuttle of the United States
<tan>, here a school class, and <li>, four, written as one word: the fourth standard, the highest class of the old Zolai schools
plural of <Singtangmi>: the people of the hills, used for the tribal peoples of Manipur
the taking of a person's name on the list, from <min>, name, and <sanna>, acceptance: above all {UN minsanna}, registration and recognition as a refugee by the UNHCR
<kawm>, here hire or rent, and <thei>, can, written as one word; after <ki>, {ki kawmthei} says in notices that a hall or a car can be hired
word of songs used with <pak> or <paak>, bloom: {lambang pak} is blossom, flourish, be in one's prime
a sound that is heard, a noise; {thawm za} is hear a sound and {thawm bawl} make a noise; also part of personal and clan names
<zonsak>, seek for someone, with the noun suffix {-na}: looking for and getting something for others, as in {nasep zonsakna}, finding work for people, a job placement service

officer of the roads and public works department who directs the building of roads and bridges; one article sets the rank beside an assistant township officer, and people use the word for any sub-assistant engineer
<tung> and <thak> written as one word: have newly arrived, of goods or people; {hong tungthak te} are the newcomers
<hun>, <leh> and <mual> written as one word, literally time and hill: the time and the circumstances in which something is done or said, the right occasion or the context
<lungzuan> with the noun suffix <na>: the heavy heart of one who misses a person or a home, loneliness or sorrow
older name of <Bago>, a city and region of lower Myanmar north-east of Yangon
<dawi> and <kungpu> written as one word: the chief of the evil spirits, in the old tales the one with whom the hero Ngal Ngam contests in magic
<mim> and <bang> written as one word, a phrase of songs used with <pian> or <piang>, be born: {mimbang pianna} is the place of one's birth, the homeland
<kingah> and <ta> written as one word: has now been obtained, is now to be had, common in headlines
<in> and <ka> written as one word: the marker <in> that closes a phrase or clause, followed by <ka>, I or my, which belongs to the next word
<a> and <kiseh> written as one word: that which is appointed, fixed or reckoned as something
the head teacher of a school, mostly written with a capital after the name or kind of the school; the Zolai word is <sangsiapi>
mathematics as a school subject
name of the town and its college in a serial story of the articles, not a real place as far as the sentences show; seems to be Zomi with the Burmese word for town
<nong> and <gen> written as one word: you tell me or us, you say to me
<kha>, <khin> and <zong> written as one word after a verb: has already happened to do it, too; {asim khakhinzong mi} are people who have already read it as well

terms: quite a few/a good number/considerable/fairly many
definition: placed after a noun, often with <mah> or <khat>: a fair number or amount of it, not few
<up>, <leh> and <saanna> written as one word, believing and accepting: what a person holds to be true, a belief or conviction; here <saanna> is from <saan>, accept, not the casting of lots
village in the Tedim area of the Chin Hills, known in the old stories for its chief Sung Hang
used after <thu>: {thu khunpi} is <thukhunpi> written as two words, the constitution of a country

a thin growth or layer that covers a surface: {paan kai} is be overgrown with moss, and of bees it is the capping over the brood cells; the dictionary data has {tui paan} for water weed. It is also part of personal names
{kel}, goat, with <pi>, mother or female: a full-grown female goat, kept for milk; the male is <keltal>
<dan>, law, with <bu>, book, and <pi>, great: the constitution of a country, in the articles the 2008 constitution of Myanmar

one's own, or by oneself, placed before a noun or a verbal noun: {mahni inn} is one's own home and {mahni kivaihawmna} self-rule; found mostly in articles written in the northern, Paite, way, where the usual Zolai is <eima> or <amah>
a life of ease and gladness, happy days or merrymaking; a word of songs and of elevated prose, compare <nopna>
a people of the Middle East living in Turkey, Syria, Iraq and Iran
a people of Meghalaya in north-east India, around Shillong, and their language; {Khasi gam} is the Khasi Hills
<hun> and <zong> written as one word: the time also, there are also times when

old Zomi custom of refuge, from <sutpi> and <pom>: one in danger of being killed runs into the house of the chief or of his enemy and clasps the main post, and is then spared; also the act of doing so
<kan>, search, with the ending <pih>: join in looking for someone or something; {hong kanpih un} in notices of missing persons is please help us look
the young men, six to nine of them, appointed at a <tonh> feast to call the guests and to bring and kill the mithun; named together with the <tuitawi>, the girls who fetch water
<kicih> and <ding> written as one word: to be called by a name, as in {Zomi kicihding}, being called Zomi
a town beside Tulsa in Oklahoma, USA, whose public schools many Zomi children attend
a tree of the warm low country, named beside {zosing}, the tree of the cold hills; in songs and sayings a figure of what is green and flourishing
word of songs and stories said after <tong>, speech: {tong luansiam} is one whose words flow well, a praise name of a young woman; also found as a personal name
word of songs for one of the Zo people or for what is Zo, as in {Zotawi Lianu}, the Zo maiden, the title of a Zomi film
expressive word after a verb, of hair, wires or matters that are tangled, jumbled or all over the place
<kul> and <te> written as one word, after a verb: the ones for whom it is necessary, those who need it or the things that must be done
a person who belongs to Christ, a believer in Christ
the becoming of one body: the wedding by which a man and a woman are joined in marriage, usually held in a church
<man>, payment, and <ngenlo>, not ask for, written as one word: without asking any payment, free of charge
a person or thing that is good to look at and copy
an administrative division of a state around its main town, written after the name as in {Tedim Khuapiseh}, Tedim township
expressive word after a verb, of something large or many that sits, lies, falls or is set down in plain view
a free computer operating system
<den>, always, and <ta>, here the word for what is now so, written as one word after a verb: always from now on, without end; common in blessings before <hen>
the Naga people, <Naga> with the plural ending <te>
<vai>, affair, and <thak>, new, as one word: a new matter to take up, a new plan or undertaking
<thei>, be able, and <dia>, the question word of spoken style, written as one word at the end of a question: can it be, could you
<a> and <thokik> written as one word: he rises again, or before a noun the one who has risen, as in {athokik Topa}, the risen Lord
the foot of a house post and the footing it stands on; also what something rests on, as in {sum khuambul}, a financial base
<thu>, matter, and <hangin>, because of, written as one word after <hih> or <tua>: because of this matter, for that reason
a bitter vegetable fruit grown in the Chin Hills and eaten cooked or dried, named with <manta>, the aubergine; the small-seeded kind is {samphok malneu}
go on living and standing as a people, a language or a name, not die out or be lost among others
being the same throughout, in word and deed and from beginning to end; the state of being even and in balance
word of songs and poetry for <tagah>, an orphan, one who has lost mother or father
the family name of the Buddha, Siddhartha Gautama, founder of Buddhism
in Zomi belief the smallest kind of spirit, with legs that are not even, said to make rich the person it befriends
of a face or person that is not known or cannot be made out; {sanggam melmak hun} is dusk, the time when the face of a brother cannot be told
a Zomi news and community website
the German people, <German> with the plural ending <te>
the talking over of a matter together
another word, other wording or another language; {kamdang khatin gen leng} is to put it in other words
<na> and <sang>, accept, written as one word: you accept, or with <na.3> of earlier time, accepted
the noun ending {-na} cut off from its word and written together with <sang>, than, usually before <in>: {phattuam nasang in} stands for {phattuamna sangin}, rather than benefit
the editing of video or sound recordings, named as a skill or a task beside video and music

terms: beer offering to the mother's family/zukholh
definition: custom in which the children of a daughter, <tute>, carry <zu> to the family of their mother, <pute>, and ask for their blessing; also written {zu kholh}
<sawl>, leafy branch, and <bang>, like, written as one word in songs, nearly always before <hei>, turn: {sawlbang hei} is to wander, to roam from place to place
song word for the light of day, said with <val> or <vaal>: {taikhua val} is day breaks
a disease of old age in which memory is lost, usually said as {Alzheimer natna}
a village named in the histories of the chiefs, a home of the Hualngo forefathers
<kik>, again or back, and the linking <a>, and, written as one word after a verb: did it again, and; went back, and
<hipah> and the sentence ending <hi> written as one word: it is simply so, that is just what it is
<sial>, mithun, with <kop>, pair: two mithun killed together at a feast of the old custom; {sialkop go} is to give such a feast
a measure for the size of a mithun, used when a mithun is named as bride price, fine or tribute; one article explains it as a hand measure of about six <letmat.1>
<Korea> and <mi>, person, written as one word: the people of Korea

terms: driving out of evil spirits/spirit chasing
definition: <kau>, evil spirit, with <bet>, strike: the rite of the old religion at the Khuado festival in which evil spirits are beaten and driven out of the village
rank of a junior officer in the army of British India and of India, written as a title before a name
sentence-final word of spoken and song style, apparently a short form of <ding> with a closing vowel, often after <kha>: will, will probably, I wonder if it will
a peak 1656 metres high between the lands of Tuimui and Selbung villages, once worshipped by the first settlers of Tuimui; as a common noun {vumpi} is a mound or heaped hill
<a> and <lunglutte> written as one word: the people who are interested, at the head of a notice that gives a contact
<hi>, be, and <tah.2> written as one word at the end of a thought, often before <cih> or <ci-in>: it is so then, it is so after all
the idea and movement of holding to the name <Zomi> and to the unity of the Zo people, a word coined with the English ending
<khua>, village, with <kip>, firm: a settlement that has become a lasting village of its own, or has been recognized as one by the ruler or the government
<vok>, pig, with <tal.3>, male: a male pig, often the pig killed at a feast
<pem>, move to live elsewhere, with <thak>, new: a person who has newly moved into a country or village
<a>, <khang.2> and <khin> written as one word, that has already progressed: {akhangkhin gamliante} are the developed great nations
a city in <Germany>, in full Frankfurt am Main
a town in <Massachusetts> where the Pilgrims from England settled; also in the name of the Plymouth Brethren and of churches
an armed group of the <Karen> people in Myanmar, known by the initials of its English name
a society for the keeping and raising of Zomi culture, known by the initials of its English name
<a> and <kileekkim>, a spelling of <kilekkim>, written as one word: that is balanced, in which nothing is too much or too little
<kidang.2>, differ, with the noun ending {-na}: the way in which one person or thing is unlike another, often paired with <kibatna>, likeness

<hoih>, good, with <muhna>, seeing: seeing things as good, glossed by the writers as optimism and set against {siatmuhna}, pessimism; one writer uses it critically, for taking as good what is not good
go forward, make progress, said of work, learning or a people; {masawn sak} is push forward
feel shame or embarrassment before others, hesitate out of shyness; {kisuanglah sak} is put someone to shame
<sam>, hair, with <kang>, white: hair turned grey or white with age, also said of a person, grey-haired
<mang> and <ding> written as one word: will obey, to be obeyed; after another verb <mang> is away or completely, as {that mangding}, will kill off

<hah>, clear or cut back, and <lo>, not, written as one word; known from the proverb {inn gua hahlo gam gua hah}, clearing the bamboo of the wild and not the bamboo at home, said of those who work for others and neglect their own
<to>, onward, and <suak>, through, written as one word after a verb: the action carries on without a break or goes on from that point
<vaimim>, maize, boiled soft as porridge, a common Zomi dish eaten with chilli; compare <buhciim>, rice porridge
<busa>, settle, with the prefix <ki>: of people who have moved, settle down and live in a place
<a> and <piasa> written as one word: the ones who have already given, in lists of donors
<ka> and <lam> written as one word: mostly in {kalam en}, I expect, where <lamen> is split by the writer; also I built, and my way or my direction

terms: not at all/by no means/not really
definition: emphatic negative placed after a verb, most often <hi>: it is by no means so, not really so, written {saamlo} or with a hyphen before the ending
<mai>, front, with the place ending <a> written on the word: in front of, in the presence of, ahead of
<suut>, go through point by point, with the prefix <ki>: of a history, a genealogy or a subject, be traced, set out or analysed
<keel>, goat, written short, with <sa>, meat: the meat of a goat
take or bring a person along to a place, lead the way for someone; {zi pui} is bring home a wife; in the articles also a part of personal names
<hausa>, chief, with the ending {-pi}, great: the principal chief or headman of a village, town or ward
a strongly scented garden herb whose leaves season soup, meat and fish and are taken as a home medicine; the English name of the plant is not settled by the articles
in songs and poetic prose with <kai>: the haze that draws across the hills in the dry season
said after <innsung> or <inn>: the circle of relatives who hold the customary roles in the affairs of a household, the family and its kin as an organised body
through the whole of life or through all generations, for ever, set against <khangkhat>, one lifetime; also written <khantawn>
<hizah>, this much, with the linking <a>, written as one word before a describing word or a verb: so, to such an extent as this
<Vuandok> with <pa>, man: the township officer as a person, a title of office
of a bomb, a grenade or a building: go off or be blown apart with a blast; {puaktam sak} is blow up
the hunt that the men of a village go on together on the morning after the Tual sacrifice of the <Sialsawm> festival, a custom of the old religion
town on the <Chindwin> in <Sagaing> Region of Myanmar, under British rule the seat of the Deputy Commissioner of the Upper Chindwin district
written iZomi: Zomi R&B and hip hop music group of three young men, formed in 2010 and based in <Tulsa> in the United States

<na> and <sung> written as one word: within you, inside you; in other sentences the noun ending {-na} of the verb before it is written onto <sung>, as {a om nasung pan}, from among those that there are
<pah>, at once, and the linking <a>, and, written as one word after a verb: does it at once, and then the next clause follows
<si>, blood, with <sitna>, test: a blood test, and the medical check that refugees and migrants take before resettlement
<hong> and <pang> written as one word; mostly in {ma hongpang}, which is <mapang>, contribute, with <hong> inside it: came forward to help with money or effort
<a> and <pawlten> written as one word: he or it and those on the same side as the doers of the action, as {US leh apawlten}, the US and its allies
putting into practice what has been said, planned or promised, action as against words
plural of <pawlmi>: the members of a group, association or church
<na> and <mit> written as one word: your eye, your eyes
<a> and <hampha> written as one word: the fortunate one, is fortunate
word of songs and poetry for <khut>, the hand or arm; {banzaal len} is hold hands
<uum>, surround, with <khawm>, together: sit together around one dish or table and eat from it, as in {ankuang uumkhawm}
the short line that joins two words or parts of a word in writing
the side where the sun rises, the east; {suahlam Zogam} is eastern Zogam
do what has been planned or agreed until it is done, carry it through
<palikte>, the police, with the subject marker <in> shortened and written as one word: the police, as the doer of the action
<hopsawn>, share and pass on, with the noun ending {-na}: the passing on to others of what one has learned or gone through, as an experience or good news
a number written as a figure, also the number of an item in a list or on a jersey
<khaak>, happen to, and <leh>, if, written as one word after a verb: if it should happen that, in case; with <ci-in> it gives the reason for a precaution
a body of ideas or the way a matter runs: writers gloss it as theory and, in {Pasian thuluan}, as theology; {thuluan zia} is the way a matter or a text runs
the comfort shown to a bereaved family by a group or its members, in words or as money; {gaalna sum} is condolence money
village of the Paite in the east of Mizoram, India, near Mimbung and <Hiangmun>
village in the east of Mizoram, India, between <Teikhang> and Mimbung
found only in the pair {vuihtheih khamtheih}, drugs and intoxicants, where it stands in the place of <guihtheih>
<teng>, dwell, with <den>, always: live in a place for good; in teaching on the Holy Spirit, dwell within the believer
<na> and <sinna> written as one word: your studies, what you learn
the raised open platform, <tau>, of the <innka> at the front of a traditional house, where people sit and talk
word of Paite and related speech for a thing or matter, where Tedim says <na> or <thu>; found in articles written in Paite
word of Paite speech for leaders, <heutu> with the plural <te>, where Tedim says <makaite>
the life a person or a people lives; {khotang hinkhua} is social life
country in West Africa
<kisai>, concern, with <a> written on to it: after <tawh>, {tawh kisaia} is concerning, that has to do with
<dah>, mourn, with <khawm>, together: share the grief of others; <tawh> marks those one mourns with
<vanlam>, the air, and <tawh>, with, written as one word: by air, said in war news of attacks made from aircraft
the English plural of <bishop>, used as written, often with the plural <te> after it
town in the north of Syria on the border with Turkey, fought over in 2014 and 2015
the cast of mind that a person or a people carries: {khuapimi lungpuak} is a civic mind and {minam lungpuak} the spirit of a people
apparently a verb for be worn out or spent, not the number <tul>, with <ta>, now: has become worn out, said of land that no longer bears and of strength; frequent in songs with <gam>, land
<hong> and <hilhna> written as one word: what it teaches us, the teaching of the church or of Scripture
expressive word placed after a verb such as <om> or <kizuak>, showing that there is a great deal of something or that it is found in large numbers
the traditional woven skirt, <nik>, of Zomi women, named beside <Zopuan>
<khasia>, be troubled in spirit, with the prefix <ki>: feel hurt or saddened by what has happened; {kikhasia sak} is upset someone

terms: as it is/as it really is
definition: <a>, <hi> and <bang> written as one word: as it is, in the way a thing really is, often followed by <in> or <lian>
word of songs, apparently the children of others, people not one's own: {singta gam} is a foreign land, the land of others
city and prefecture in the north-east of Japan, known for the nuclear power plant damaged in 2011

terms: be able to love/manage to love
definition: <it>, love, and <zo>, be able, written as one word: be able to love, go on loving; with <nawnlo> or <hetlo>, be unable to love
<i> and <mu> written as one word: we see, we find
<khaam>, forbid or hold back, with the noun ending {-na}: a prohibition or a thing that holds back; {nat khaamna zatui} is medicine that prevents illness
<a> and <kisuun> written as one word, after <tawh>, with: that which resembles, similar to
form of <tangsam>, lack, mostly written after a separate <ki> as {ki tangsap}, the same as <kitangsap>: be needed, what one needs
word of songs for <khuang>, the drum, named with the gong and the cloth of the forefathers; one writer derives it from <len> with {lensialki} and {lenpuan}
<Aizawl> and <ah> written as one word: in Aizawl, to Aizawl
<nong> and <hawh> written as one word: you visit us, you come to see us; found only in the closing line of one news site

terms: regard as good/look on with favour
definition: <hoih>, good, with <muh>, see: take a thing to be good; one writer sets it against {a hoihna mu}, see the good that is in a thing, and uses it of calling good what is not
coffee, the plant and its beans; {kaphi kung} is the coffee tree and {kaphi tang} the coffee bean
a gourd grown in the fields beside <mai.5>, the pumpkin, and eaten as a vegetable; when ripe its skin is covered with a white powder
a young unmarried woman, paired with <tangval>, young man; the same as <nungak>
<thumaan> and <thutak> written as one word: the truth, what is true and right

word of songs placed before <zuun> or <zom>, as {giabang zuun}, put a land or a people in order again, build it up; a comparison with <bang>, like, whose first part {gia} is not explained by the sentences
a town in the state of Assam in India, the seat of Eastern Theological College
the Mormon church, the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, and its members
<theih> and <tawp.4> written as one word: the most that can be done; {ka theihtawp in} is as best I can, and after a describing word, as {a manlang theihtawp in}, as quickly as possible
a city in Germany, the capital of West Germany from 1949
word of songs for <mual>, the hills and ridges on the skyline where the sun rises and sets; {lenmual dawn} is the hilltops
word of songs for <singkung>, a tree, as a list of song words explains it; {tulsing dawn} is the top of a tree
put things, goods or ideas of several people together in one place or into one whole
<Yangon> and <ah> written as one word: in Yangon, to Yangon
<si.2>, blood, with <sit.2>, examine: a test of the blood; of people leaving for another country, the medical examination before the journey
<simlei>, the world, with <vai.2>, affair: the affairs of the world, which writers explain as politics; also written {SimleiVai}
<a> and <liim> written as one word: its shadow or shade; in news writing more often its picture or image, set beside <athu>, the text
a bridge over a river or a gorge; {sikkhau leidawh} is a suspension bridge; also the name of a place in the Tedim area
<i> and <na.3> written as one word before a verb: we, with the particle that sets the action in an earlier time, as {ina om hi}, we were
<cih.2> and <peen> written as one word after a statement or question: as for the matter that, marking the whole clause before it as the topic
the planet Saturn; also the Roman god after whom Saturday is named, and a kind of American space rocket
<ka> and <om> written as one word: I am, I stay; before a noun, where I am

terms: long for/miss/want more/be loath to part
definition: feel that one has not had enough of a person or of a good time: miss someone, long for more, be unwilling to stop or leave; paired with <iplah> and <ngaklah>
word of songs for <sum> and <dangka>, money, as a list of song words explains it; {sesum minthang} is wealth and fame
placed after a verb of shining, rising or seeing: bright and clear to the eye, as the sun that rises or glows red, or an aim seen plainly
a village of the Tedim area, in the Tungzang village tract
a village and village tract in the Simzang area of the Tedim region, named after its first headman
the act or place of rolling up or gathering together; {kha hualna} is the rite of calling and binding the souls of a married couple at the Ton feast, and {kithu hualna} is agreement
an exclamation of dismay, pity, longing or surprise, a fuller form of <kalai>
to fly away to another place, as a bird does; commonly said of people who leave to resettle in another country
a lit torch carried at night, and the carrying of it; {khuahaang meide} or {khuasia meide} is a will-o'-the-wisp, a ghost light

terms: in the long run/after a long time/eventually
definition: usually as {a sawtteh}: as time goes on, in the end
one who teaches or preaches, chiefly a teacher of religious doctrine
plural of <laisiam>: those who are educated or good at study

terms: pleasant to talk with/enjoyable in conversation
definition: pleasant to talk with; also said of people talking happily together

terms: act separately/go one's own way/stand apart
definition: to act apart from the group instead of together with it

terms: all the siblings/all the relatives/brothers and sisters
definition: <sanggam> with <teng>, all: the whole circle of brothers, sisters and relatives
<i> and <suah> written as one word: we become, we turn into
a region of South Asia, a state of India and a province of Pakistan
adverb of small degree or size, as in {neu ciuciau}, tiny, and {hi ciuciau lel}, to be merely
to have the advantage or benefit of something
<a> and <kidang> written as one word: that is different, that differs
the charismatic revival movement that came from Mizoram, Mizo hlimsang, and its followers, found within several churches, marked by ecstatic dancing in worship
plural of <minampih>
to be poisoned by something eaten or drunk, or to be poisonous
the people who come from Dim village, {Dim Khua}, and their descendants

terms: driving out of evil spirits/spirit chasing
definition: the driving of evil spirits out of house and village with torches and noise at the Khuado festival
taking part in or attending another's occasion in support; {ki uapna} is attending one another's feasts and funerals
the large valued bead of the traditional Zomi necklace, counted as {khipi tang}, a bead, and {khipi gui}, a string
the Korean autumn harvest festival, compared in the articles to the Zomi Khuado festival
a village, in English spelling usually Khuangleng, whose warriors fought the Laaitui people in the nineteenth century
those who were among the first to do something
a bird; the form of <vasa> with its parts in the other order, said in the articles to be the usage of Mizo and other dialects
a higher or further step, an advance; mostly in {kalsang suan}, to take a step forward
word of songs and poetry, literally like salt, used with <dah> for deep grief and with <mang> for being lost
to clap the hands, and the clapping itself
<lut> and the particle <ta> written as one word: has now entered, has joined
to manage the use of time; at a meeting or programme, to act as moderator or master of ceremonies, and the person who does so
<hi>, be, and the particle <tazen> written as one word, placed after a verb or describing word and before <hi> or <uh>: it really is so, it actually is so, said with surprise or reproach
plural of <gualzawhna>: victories, and the things a person has achieved
<ci>, say, and <giap>, outright, written as one word after the words quoted: say it firmly and without holding back
<en>, look, and the ending <lehang>, if we, written as one word: if we look at, when we consider, used to bring in an example or a point of view
<om>, be, and the emphatic particle <se> written as one word, mostly before <lo>: {omse lo} is there is none at all, there is no such thing
the air force of a country, named beside the army and the navy
<tu>, this, and <hunteh>, at the time, written as one word: at this time, nowadays, often set against <nidang>, formerly
<a> and <kaang> written as one word: white, the white one; {avom akaang}, the black and the white, is said of all kinds without distinction and of how a matter really stands
<la>, song, with <dawng>, the counting word for songs: a single song or poem as one composed piece
name of a Zomi news magazine published at Aizawl in Mizoram, taken from the name of the bird
a bird of the Zo hills whose loud repeated call is heard in the dry season and towards evening, named beside {tangawm} or <tawlawk>; the species is not determined
of a person or a way of thinking: like someone from a remote village, unpolished, narrow and behind the times; also such a person
<gam>, country, with <seh>, part: one of the states or provinces into which a country is divided, as Shan State or Queensland; a word of a few writers for what is mostly called state
a thorough overturning of the order and way of thinking of a society, the word one writer uses for English revolution; its last part is <lumleh>, turn over, with the noun ending {-na}
<lah>, show, and <pakding>, to do briefly, written as one word and mostly followed by {-in}: to show it briefly, for example; a word of one writer, who also shortens it to {lpd}
<tangko>, proclaim, with <pih>: make a message or a cause known to people, speak up publicly for it; {a tangkopih pawl} are those who campaign for something
<tonkhop>, go together with, with the noun ending {-na}: going along together with someone, as in {Pasian tawh tonkhopna}, walking with God
town and district in the Magway Region of central Myanmar, on the Ayeyarwady river
name of a Linux operating system for computers, made by the company Canonical

<taang>, millet, with <tang>, seed: a single grain of millet; the saying {taangtang phelhawm}, split a grain of millet and share it, from the tale of Thang Ho and Lian Do, stands for sharing even the least thing in love
a dictionary, mostly as {tongdot bu} with <bu>, book; in old songs the word is also found of spoken words
<beh>, clan, and <khat>, one, written as one word: one single clan, people of the same clan or kin; also said of things that are of one kind
plural of <Kuki>: the Kuki people
