<minam>, people, with <neu>, small: a people that is small in number within a country, an ethnic minority
city near Tokyo in Japan and the international airport of Tokyo that lies there
a traditional Zomi woven cloth with its own pattern, worn by men and given as a mark of honour, named beside <Puanlaisan> and {Tualpuan}; also shirts and coats sewn from it
a traditional Zomi feast of several days in the old religion at which much <zu>, beer, is drunk, named beside the {Ton} feast and the feasts {gal aih} and {sa aih}
<thum>, three, with <gawm>, join: three joined in one, said of God as Father, Son and Holy Spirit, {thumgawm Pasian}, the triune God; alone it stands for the Trinity
help given to those in need, above all money or goods given as aid; it is used as <huhna> is and may be the same word in another spelling
after the name of a pest or of what is guarded: keeping birds, insects or mosquitoes away, or a means of doing so, as {vasa hunna}, something against birds, and {lo hunna}, the guarding of a field
the sugar cane plant and its sweet stalk; {kawltu tui} is cane juice
city in the Philippines, named for the seminaries where Zomi pastors studied

word of the custom {ngawk sat} of the Khuado feast, for which the young men gather at their youth house at midday and then wrestle, and of the call {ngawk ngawk e} that the elders of the house raise first; what the word itself names is not clear from the texts
city in Libya, in the news of the war against IS
a frog, written beside <uiphuk> as another word for it
word of songs and love poems for the heart or mind as the seat of longing and thought, from <lung>, heart
the separate gate or opening of a traditional Zomi house by which the mithun and cattle go into their pen under the house, from <sial>, mithun, and <kong>, door
placed after a verb: after sit, ride or set on top, up high where all can see; after say or record, openly and plainly
<nasep>, work, with the ending {-pi}, great or chief: the main work or chief task of a person or body
<kikum> and <ding> written as one word: will discuss, are to confer about
<tam> and <simsim> written as one word: quite many, a considerable number
{a zat beh toh} written as one word: use a thing further, go on using it beyond the time first agreed; it begins with <azat> and ends with <toh>
silk thread and what is made of it, from <khau>, thread; in the notices {Zodial naikhau} is a Zomi scarf of silk
<gam> and <ten> written as one word: the countries, as the doer of the action

terms: go one's own way/stand apart/be self-willed
definition: keep to one's own way or opinion apart from the others and not join in with them; {thu tangpek} is one who is self-willed in a matter

terms: not at all/nowhere near/by no means
definition: <deksuai> and <lo> written as one word, after a verb or describing word: not at all, far from it
a level or flat piece of land among the hills, from <mun>, place
<kik> and <lo> written as one word, after a verb: not again, not back; {nung kiklo} is not turning back and {dawng kiklo} is not answering
<ki> with <zik>: of a road, a path or the site of a village, be laid out and made
<lo>, field, and <bang>, like, written as one word, a comparison of songs and sayings: {lobang tul} is grow old and worn out like a used field, and {lobang khual} is care for as for a field
<a> and <lianbel> written as one word: the greatest, the highest; {Alianbel Siampipa} is the High Priest and is also said of the Pope
only in the pair {sanpi sanno}, illness great and small, which the texts explain as {natpi natneu}; see <sanno>
<san>, red, with the ending {-pi}, great: of a robe or garment, deep red; apart from this the word is a personal name
<zaw>, more, and <a>, and, written as one word at the end of a clause that another clause follows
{Kawl galkap} written as one word and with long vowels: the army of Myanmar or its soldiers
ending of colloquial speech placed after the verb at the end of a statement, giving it emphasis or feeling; it holds the word <cia> of the same use
the bank of earth that stands above a road on its uphill side, where the road is cut into a slope; from <lam>, road, and <phung>, bank
<palai>, envoy, with the ending {-pi}, chief, written with long vowels: the ambassador of a country, also the chief representative of a state or body
a Zomi village of the Tedim area, named with Dimpi, Dimlo and Suangpi and written after the names of people who come from it
live or act at the side of others and in dependence on them, as a small people does in the land or the party of another; also one who so depends; from <pang>, side, and <bel>, cling to
<hel> and <loh> written as one word: not mixed in, not included, left out; {tui helloh} is undiluted, pure
<hong> and <kihel> written as one word: come and take part, join in
<nih>, <leh> and <thum> written as one word: two or three, a few
<nga>, fish, and <bang>, like, written as one word, a comparison of songs: {ngabang leng} is live and play happily together like fish in the water
<pom>, hold, with <siam>, skilled: know how to accept a thing and take it in good part, whether criticism, a loss or a chance
<in>, placed after the doer or after a verb, and the following <hong> written as one word
exclamation of colloquial speech: at the start, hey or oh; written after the last word of a statement with a hyphen, it gives the statement feeling
<kinaih> with the ending {-na}: the state of being close or akin, of persons, peoples or languages
a cool gentle wind, from <huih>, wind, and <dam>, cool
poetic word of songs and laments for the face or looks of a loved person, as in {na sakmel muh ding}, to see your face
<kisin>, practise or learn, with its last part said twice: go on practising or learning over a length of time
<a>, its, and <tong> written as one word, the second word of the pair {azia atong}: the ways and character of a person or a thing
<a> with <tong>, here a form of the verb for holding the traditional feast of merit: one who has held the feast, {atong lote} those who have not
word of traditional songs for a bamboo that grows in clumps at the edge of the village, a picture of people growing and thriving together, the last part is <gua>, bamboo
poetic word of songs for a young person or the time of youth, mostly in {seino gual}, young companions, and {ka seino lai}, when I was young
<i>, we, and <siam>, be skilled, written as one word: we know how to, we are good at
the English word used in Zolai articles for the movement and thinking that seeks equal standing for women, explained as {numei lapsangna}
<bual>, bathe or wallow, with the ending {-na}: the place of bathing or wallowing, {tui bualna} is a swimming pool or bathing place
poetic word of songs for the many people, the whole company, often after <mi>

terms: up to standard/on a par/abreast of others
definition: <gual>, peers, with <ban>, reach: reaching the level of others, up to the standard of the time, said of work, music, a town or a way of thinking
<gelhsak>, have something written, and <nop>, want, written as one word: want a letter or paper to be written for one
<nun>, life, with <lui>, old: the life one lived before, former ways, the days gone by, {nunlui sial} is recall the past
<kau>, the harmful spirit of the old belief, and <nei>, have, written as one word: a person or family said to keep such a spirit, feared and avoided in marriage
<ma>, front, with the <bang> of song language, before verbs of striving and beginning such as <pang>: go forward, press on or make a beginning together
word of song language placed before <khang>, grow, with the comparing <bang>, like: {kilbang khang} is grow up well, thrive and increase, said of children, a people or a land
<gawmkhawm>, put together into one, with the linking <in>: joining or combining things, and so doing what follows
<simsim>, rather or fairly, with the plural <te>, after a describing word: those who are fairly so, as {gol simsimte}, the rather large ones
<sim>, read, said twice, with the plural <te>, after <lai>: those who read much or keep on reading
<zah>, amount, and <tek>, each, written as one word after a verb: as much as each one wants or is able
the people of a village or a people as a body and their common life, {khuatang nuntakzia} is social life and {khuatang kipawlna} civil society
<neih>, have, with an ending that means leaving behind: take another wife, husband or lover and so leave the one that one had, after {zi dang}, {pasal dang} or {lawmnu dang}
<guai>, the word of address to equals, with the plural <te>: friends, said at the end of a sentence or as {guaite aw}
former province of China east of Tibet, the region of Kham, named in an article on where the Zomi came from as the Sikang-Tibetan Plateau
the English title of the person who calls and leads a committee, written before or after a name in lists of office bearers
<na>, you, and <san>, the form of <sang>, receive, written as one word: you receive or accept, as {thupha nasan}, you receive blessing
placed after a noun to mark an extreme or unexpected case, the same as <nangawn>
the Burmese word for politics, the affairs of state and party, set against the work of the church in the articles
a village in the township of Kalaymyo, one of the places that received rice after the floods
<tui>, water, with a second part that means go under: covered by flood water, said of houses, villages and valleys, {tuitup cip} is completely under water

the yearly rite of the old religion in which the village honours its guardian spirit at the <tual>, also called {Tualbia}, kept with a village taboo and at the same time as <Sialsawm>, {Tualbawl kha} is the month in which it falls
<upa>, leader, with <phual>, place: the office of an organisation or of the authorities, a word of some writers who gloss it with English office

terms: opening day/first day of a feast
definition: the day on which a traditional feast begins, as the first day of <Khuado> and the day the mithun is killed at a feast of merit, said as {pansik ni}
a traditional Zomi garment of plain cotton worn by men, named with <Puanlaisan> among the cloths of the people
<dawi>, demon, and <lut>, enter, written as one word: the state of being possessed by a spirit, or a person in that state
cook grain soft, alone or with meat, and the dish so made, as {taksih nganhuan}, the grain dish eaten with meat at the old feasts, and {aksa nganhuan} with chicken
be at ease in spirit, feel safe and content, often as {khalum tuam}, feel relieved, and {khalumna} is comfort
in news reports after a number of people: lose their lives, be killed, set beside <liam>, be injured

<lawm>, friend or companion, and <ding>, to be, written as one word: one who is to be a friend or companion, {khansung lawmding} and {khantawn lawmding} are a partner for life, a future husband or wife
<panmunlen>, office bearer, with the plural <te>: the people who hold the offices of an organisation
rank of an officer of the army, police or civil service shown by two pips, a lieutenant, the step below <bawkthum>
the Japanese form of wrestling, in {sumo kimawlte}, sumo wrestlers, and {sumo kibuan}, wrestle sumo; a Japanese word

terms: make a living/earn a living/seek a livelihood
definition: seek what one eats, from <nek>, food to eat, and <zong>, seek: work for a living, or the living so made
<khin>, finished or already, and the linking <a> written as one word: stands after a verb, the action is already done, and the sentence goes on
plural of <tangta>, in the pair {tangpi tangtate}, the general public

a small bird that comes in the cold season and is known for its bobbing, dancing walk, named in songs as a sign of winter; probably the wagtail; Lailen is also the name of a village in the story of Liando
of the weather, fine and clear, without cloud or rain; said when the rain clouds have gone, the opposite of <khuasia>; Khuapha is also the name of a village
<hong> and <sat> written as one word: found a village or pitch a camp, strike or beat; of the sun, beat down, and of the clock, strike the hour
<ong> and <nei> written as one word: come to have, as children or land, or hold, as a speech or a wedding
<na> and <lungsim> written as one word: your heart, your mind
plural of <zinmang>: the invited guests of a festival or conference
<ong> and <kipan> written as one word: begin, set out from
<a> and <dikna> written as one word: his righteousness, or what is right in something; known from the verse on seeking the kingdom of God and his righteousness
<nui>, laugh, with the prefix {ki-}: people laugh, a company laughs together, often followed by a word painting the sound such as <ziahziah>
said with the prefix {ki-} and <tawh>, with: be contrary to, go against, be at odds with; apparently a picture from <keel> <ki>, the horns of a goat, which point apart
<nei> and <in> written as one word and shortened: having, and with that; the same as <neiin>
word of songs for the people in their hundreds, the multitude, from <mi>, people, and <za> in its meaning hundred; Miza is also the name of a village with a school
a village and quarter of Lamka, Churachandpur, in Manipur, India, and the stream of the same name
<tulaitak>, now, with the linking <a> that joins it to the following word: the present, the one of now
<nitumna>, west, and <lam>, side or direction, written as one word: the west, the western side of a place
stands after a describing word: thin, sparse or of little account, as hair growing thinly, land lying bare, or a place that is only a tiny village, {khuano thilthel}
word painting the manner of something small or of one who acts alone and quietly: {neu keukeu} is very small, {tai keukeu} is scamper along, {om keukeu} is stay all by oneself
<kikeuh>, at all, and <lo>, not, written as one word: stands after a verb, not in the least
plural of <Vaphual>, the great hornbill, emblem of the Zomi
being old or senior, the form of <upa> used before another word: {upat khit ciangin} is after growing old, {kum upat} is advancing age, and {upat bawlna} is treating someone as an elder, respect
<mah> and <tek> written as one word, after <kua>: {a kua matek} is each and every one, everyone without exception, common in greetings and appeals
<hilel>, be only, and the sentence ending <hi> written as one word: ends a statement, it is just that and nothing more
<gal>, <le> and <sa> written as one word: enemies and wild animals, the two dangers of life in the old villages
<mun>, place, with <lui.2>, old: the place where a village or building once stood, as {khua munlui}, an old village site
act in a film or play, perform a scene; from the Burmese word for show, which is also the first part of {piah-ta-na}, problem, and {piahzat}, a play
<khia>, out, and the sentence ending <hi> written as one word: ends a statement after a verb of saying, coming forth or beginning, as {pulak khiahi}, announced
<hi>, be, and <leltak>, merely, written as one word: it is just that, it is simply so, said with some feeling

terms: since the time of/from the generation of
definition: <khang.3>, generation, and <pan>, from, written as one word: {pupa khangpan} is since the days of the forefathers
in the night just past, from <zan>, night; often {zantak in}
in {zantak an}, the staple food, the food that a household mainly lives on, such as maize or millet
island country in the Atlantic Ocean, north of Cuba
<sa>, here already done, with the emphatic <mah>, written as one word after a verb: just as already said, hoped or done, and with <in> all the while doing so
<denciang>, later, with the marker <in>, written as one word: later on, in time to come
<kamkum>, talk over, with the noun suffix {-na}: a talking over of a matter, a conversation, or formal talks between parties
the people of Nepal and those of that descent living in India and elsewhere, and their language
a wide stretch of worked fields, <lo>, field, with <zau>, spread wide; with the name of a crop before it, land planted with that crop
make a matter or a people greater, better, wider or more important than it was, bring it forward
<ka>, I, with <seh>, set or assign, written as one word: I count someone or something as such, after a phrase ending in {-in}; with <uh> also we have appointed
<sun>, here take after or be a copy of, with the linking <a>, written as one word after {lim leh mel}, image and likeness: bearing the image of, made after the likeness of
<sun>, daytime, with the place marker <a>, written as one word: during the day
<hong>, toward the speaker or the place spoken of, with <kuan>, set out, written as one word: set out and come for a task
<ahih>, its being so, with <ban>, what comes on top, written as one word and followed by <ah>: besides being that, on top of being that
the milk of a goat, {kel}, goat, with <nawi>, milk; compare <bawngnawi>
<khangkhia>, arise or grow up, with the causative <sak>: make a leader arise for a people, or bring a child up
the highest part of something, as the ridge of a roof or the top of the world; also the name of a mountain and a stream near Saizang
go to another village or land to get food in a time of want, as the brothers of Joseph went to Egypt; also said of the people who go
name of several cities in the United States, among them the capital of Illinois, the home of Abraham Lincoln
do a thing in deed and bring it to completion, not only speak or plan; {a semsuah makai} is a leader who gets the work done with his people
leaning to one side like a scale that tips, said of a teaching, a belief or a way of seeing that holds only one side of a matter
<zuun>, tend and put in order, with <ding>, to or for, written as one word: to be maintained, for putting in order
<Tedim> and <khuapi>, town, written as one word: the town of Tedim
<tai>, run, and <kidemna>, competition, written as one word: a running race
<pu>, grandfather, <leh>, and, and <pate>, fathers, written as one word: the forefathers of a people
country on the west coast of South America
a kind of <khi>, necklace, of the Zomi, a costly ornament and heirloom named beside <khipi>
the prefix <a> with <madawk>, at the front, written as one word: the one out in front, a leading or pioneering person or thing
<khang>, grow, to the full: of a child, come of age; of a believer, grow to maturity, beside <picing>; of a disease, reach its full stage

terms: think of for/be considerate toward/look out for
definition: <khual>, be considerate of, with <sak>, for another: keep the good or the future of someone in mind and act for it
<khutlet>, take by the hand in greeting, with the prefix {ki-}, each other: shake hands with one another
word of songs and poetry, <mu>, here hawk or kite, with <bang>, like: mostly before <ngai>, long for, of deep longing for parents, home or a loved one
the opening at the bottom of the body; also a hole in the bottom of a thing, see the second sense

terms: with a hole in the bottom/holed
definition: placed after the name of a pot, a container or trousers: having a hole in its bottom or seat
a village of the Tedim area, named in a list of Zomi villages and after the names of people from it
the clear, wholesome water of the Zo land, a word of songs; also the brand name of bottled drinking water made by Zomi in Kalay
<mi>, people, and <lakah>, among, written as one word: among other people, in public
the head of a government department, of a state government or of an army, a title placed after the name of the state, department or army
of a shirt or jacket, having short sleeves, the opposite of <bansau>, long-sleeved
<hong> and <kisang> written as one word: be accepted, said by the side that receives
<sap>, call, and <man>, price, written as one word: what is paid for a telephone call
after <inn>, house: the money paid each month for a rented house or room
<kaal>, week or interval, and <sung>, in, written as one word: within a week, as {tu kaalsung}, this week, or during a span of time

terms: make known to us/let us know/reveal
definition: <hong> and <theisak> written as one word: make something known to the speaker or to us
<kihel>, be mixed, and <zau>, spread wide, written as one word: mix freely with one another, said of peoples, languages and good and bad things
the country of Egypt, in the spelling of older Bible translations
<kham>, gold, and <khuk>, pit, written as one word: a gold mine, also said of the mines in Burma where young men went to work
<a> and <tatak> written as one word: the real thing, and with <in> after it, in truth, actually
<ki>, horn, and <li>, four, written as one word, in the folk tale name {sial kili nei}, the mithun that has four horns
a town in Texas, USA, where a Zomi community lives
<zek>, spend, with the prefix {ki-}: of money, be spent or paid out for a purpose
<tuambawl>, treat differently, with the prefix {ki-}: treat one another as different, keep apart from others, or of a thing be made separately
the particle <na> before a verb and <muak>, welcome, written as one word: welcomed, came out to meet
a team ball game played indoors, in which Zomi youth teams take part in Asian championships
meat or vegetables boiled plain in water in the Zo way, without oil; {aksa Zohuan} is chicken cooked so

terms: stretching out/in a wide view/spread out
definition: placed after a verb of seeing or appearing: of a land, haze or cloud seen spread out far and wide, or of a thing seen clearly before the eyes
<va>, go and, and <kihel>, be among, written as one word: go and take part in a meeting or event
<van>, goods, and <thak>, new, written as one word: newly bought or newly made things
<van>, heaven, and <thak>, new, written as one word: the new heaven, said together with the new earth
<pua>, carry, and <zo>, be able, written as one word: be able to carry a load, or to bear wealth, poverty or fame
a place where a stream falls over a cliff; {tui zeu} is the falling water
<dat>, substance, with the plural <te>: the substances that a food, the body or the soil contains
the act of pushing a person or group aside as worthless, or the state of being so rejected

terms: the way it is/how it is/that it is
definition: <ahih>, its being, and <dan>, manner, written as one word: how something is, or the fact that it is so, after a clause that states it
the pressing of a way of thinking into the minds of people by a ruling power, glossed in the articles as brainwashing
the place where a person was born and grew up; {a lamkiatna gam} is his native land
<ten>, the plural with the marker of the doer, and <bel>, as for, written as one word: placed after a noun to say what that group for its part says or does, often in contrast
<thukhenmang>, judge, with the male ending {-pa}: the judge of a court
<a> and <tenna> written as one word: his, her or their dwelling place, the place where they live
a rocket or shell fired in war, in news of fighting
a solid piece of iron for a smith to forge; also said of the fuel rods of a nuclear reactor
<i>, our, and <pawlpi>, church, written as one word
<anneek>, eating, with the noun ending {-na}: the eating of a meal, or the food eaten; {anneekna khan} is a dining room
<tenkhop>, live together, with the noun ending {-na}: the living together of people in one house, or of different peoples in one town or country
<zawl>, sweetheart, and <lui>, old, written as one word: the person one used to court
<pai>, go or come, and <teh>, when, written as one word: when someone goes or comes

terms: be put on/be printed on/be included/be given a ride
definition: <tuangsak>, put on, with the prefix {ki-}: of words or a picture, be placed on a book, banknote or page, or be included in a law; of people, be let ride in a vehicle
<pom>, embrace, and <cip>, tightly, written as one word: hold a person tight in the arms; also hold fast to a name or an idea
<ankam>, mustard, of the kind that forms a round head: cabbage; the articles also use it for the cabbage family as a whole, with broccoli and cauliflower
a country in South America
<kong>, door, and <mai>, front, written as one word: the place in front of the door of a house, church or hall
<na>, you, and <sap> written as one word: you call or summon someone; with a room, a house or a helper, you rent or hire
the Korean dish of salted and soured cabbage, eaten with rice
the people of <Sihzang>, the name with the plural <te>
<kikhen>, be separated, and <kik>, again, written as one word: of people, part from one another again; of a thing, be divided further
<kikhen> in its meaning be printed, and <kik>, again: of a book, be printed again
the name of a Zomi restaurant in Malaysia, below the office of the Zomi Association of Malaysia; the name is also used in writing as a poetic word and as the title of a series
<a> and <theihlawh>, come to know, written as one word: he, she or they get to know something as a result
a village in Champhai district of Mizoram, India, where speakers of Tedim live
<masuan>, head for, with the prefix <ki>: set one's course and go forward, on a road or toward an aim in life
placed after a verb, <taleh>, even if, in the form for we, compare <lehang>, if we: even if we do so, wherever or however much we do
<kai>, pull, with the prefix <ki>, written with a long vowel: of tax, be levied; {kikaai khawm} is be gathered together and {kikaai awk} is be caught up or entangled
the English word agency with the Zolai plural <te>: agencies, as those that resettle refugees or that send workers abroad, and news agencies
a village and border market beside <Tamu> in Sagaing Region, Myanmar, at the crossing to Moreh in India
<khet>, print, and <sak> written as one word: print a book for someone, or have it printed
a group of people chosen to deal with a matter, the English word in Zolai spelling
<puah>, repair, and <to>, upward, written as one word: mend a thing and make it better than before, said of customs, a way of life, software or a person
<biang>, cheek, and <ah>, at, written as one word: on the cheek, mostly of tears; after a word for a door or gate, at its side
<na> and <huh>, help, written as one word: you help; with <na> in its meaning of an earlier action, he, she or they helped
the <Sialkal> hill range in the north-east of Mizoram, India, home of the Tedim and Paite speaking people of that state
a traditional food of <taang>, millet, cooked for feasts such as the Khuado festival, pressed into lumps with the hand and eaten with meat; cooking it is {taksih nganhuan}
the reading of a text before printing to find and correct its mistakes
the English pop group of the 1960s
<dawilawm>, demon, and <nei>, have, written as one word: a person who is said to have a spirit as companion
<taang>, millet, boiled soft as a porridge, often together with chicken or pork; {vaimim ciim} is the same dish made of maize
<siat>, thrust, and <in> written as one word: sticking a thing into or onto something, as a torch on the tip of a bamboo or a tree
a camp and place at the front in France where the men of the Chin Labour Corps arrived in August 1917, in the spelling of the articles
form of <luikhia> used before endings and before the noun it describes: bring a matter, a piece of writing or food out before others
word of songs for the moon, <solkha> with {-pi}, great; {tung solkhapi} is the moon above
placed after a describing word or a verb and before the closing word, it seems to strengthen it in a lively way: {lum heha} is nice and warm, {nam heha} smells strongly
word of songs, <thei>, fruit, with <bang>, like: {theibang sen} is red like ripe fruit, said of youth, and {min theibang lo} is call a name, as one plucks fruit
<a> and <hive> written as one word: it is so indeed, often followed by <maw>

the basic rule or statement on which a body, a system or a piece of teaching rests: the constitution of an organisation, named beside <thumeilet>, by-laws, the principle of a system, or the key verse of a sermon
<vua> and <leh> written as one word: if, said after a verb when several persons are meant, if you all or if they

terms: be concerned with/be involved in/relate to
definition: <kisai>, concern, with <pih>, together with: have to do with a matter; {a kisaipih} is the one concerned, the relevant person or side
<ni>, sun, with <lum>, warm: the pleasant warmth of the sun; {nilum awi} is bask in the sun, sunbathe
dance at a feast, as the young people do in the courtyard; found mostly in songs
after the name of a field of work, those who run it or deal in it: {meileng lamsai} is a railway man
<nino> and <ni> written as one word: Saturday, the day before <Nipini>, Sunday
title of Pau Cin Hau as the man through whom a script came into being, <Laipian> with <pa>, man
<a> and <kiteng> written as one word: the ones who marry, or they marry
<theihsiam>, understand, with <pih>, together with: understand another person's situation, thoughts or hardship with sympathy
<lei> and <thak> written as one word: new land, and beside {van thak}, new heaven, the new earth
<lei>, buy, and <thak> written as one word: buy something new, or one who has newly bought
<kaal> and <nih> written as one word: two weeks
word of songs and speeches, found almost only in {maciang suan}, go forward, strive ahead together

terms: pass out of sight/pass away/be gone
definition: in {mual hong khupsan}, go down behind the hill out of sight: said of a year or a time that is ending or is forgotten
placed after <ci>, say, or <hi>, be, and before the closing word; it seems to stress that the thing was really said or is really so
pour water into or over something; {zu leih} is pour water into the beer pot so that the beer can be drunk
one kind of traditional Zo song with its own tune, named beside <laphei>, <lapi> and <zawlla>
<hi> and <lam> written as one word: the fact that something is so, said after <a>, <na> or <i> and before a verb of knowing or seeing
{hih lam} said short: this direction, this side, set against {hualam}, that way
affectionate word of address used by a parent or an older person to a boy or a young man
stick out or turn upward, as the bottom or a turned-up nose; {del liangin} with a verb of running is said of making off in a hurry
<thu>, matter, with <kituahna>, meeting: a coming to one mind, an accord; {Mang Thukituahna} is the accord of the chiefs at Tedim
<it> and <loh> written as one word: not love, and one who is not loved
<ih> and <thei> written as one word: we know, we come to know
plural of <puaisa>: the agents who arrange work, papers or travel for others, also those who smuggle people
a Zomi village in the Tedim area of Chin State, Myanmar
<siam>, skilled, with <nel>, fine: skilled to a fine degree, thoroughly proficient in something learned
sound written for a pause while thinking, doubting or sighing, before or after what is said
after a place name: the country from that place southward or down toward the plains, <khang> as in <khanglam> with <siah>, and beyond
something to eat, a bare living; {neektawm zong} is seek a living
at a later time, after a while, said of what will happen or be done later
the seeds of the bean plant <ga>, shelled from the pod: beans as food, also burned and ground in making gunpowder
in {gatang kai}, literally draw the beans: weigh a matter point by point and settle it, reach a compromise
a thick, soft and warm cloth woven of cotton, used as a blanket and spread as a covering, one of the traditional cloths of the Zomi
<ding> and <ciang> written as one word after a verb: when about to do it, or only as far as doing it

terms: slaughter an animal/kill for a feast
definition: <sa> and <go> written as one word: kill an animal for a feast or a rite; {sago teng} are those who provide the animals killed
a traditional festival of the <Zomi> that some keep as the new year, another name of <Sialsawm>
a kind of <zusa>, rat, with a white breast, that multiplies in the fields after the rice harvest and is caught for food
a Zomi village in <Manipur>, India
the earning and handling of money as a field of life, the economy, glossed economic in the articles; also trade carried on for gain
<luang>, body, with <man>, price: money paid to the family of a person who has died, by a government for its servant or soldier, or by the one at fault
a Zomi village in the <Tonzang> area of Chin State, Myanmar

terms: be particular to/be directed at/focus on
definition: with {-a} or {-in} after a noun: with particular regard to it, directed at it or based on it
word of songs and love letters for the one a person loves and longs for
<khuasa>, live, with the prefix <ki>: of people, live their life or earn a living in a place or by some means
<siam>, skilled, with <zia>, manner: the way of doing something skilfully, how to do it well

terms: not even a penny/even one kyat
definition: <pekkhat> and <zong> written as one word: even a single coin, with a negative verb not even a penny
word of songs: lie down or rest, as in the arms of a loved one or in the bosom of God
<kua>, who, with <ta>: who, mostly in questions that expect the answer no one; {kuatu kuata} is anyone at all
<lim> and <sak> written as one word: make food taste good; also find something tasty, enjoy eating it
<lo>, the form of <lawh>, call a name, said twice: keep calling a name, go on using it
<ta> and <teng> written as one word: all the children of someone
title of a headmaster or senior teacher, <Sya> with <pi>, great, written before the name; the Burmese sayagyi
organisation and website that publishes leaked secret documents of governments
<hongtung> and <khin> written as one word: has already arrived at the place spoken of
a district in the east of <Singapore>
breathe noisily through the nose while asleep, from <nak>, nose
<England> with the plural <te>: the people or the government of England, the British
<deih>, want, with <zia>, manner: what a person wants and the way he wants it
<mit>, eye, with <na.4>, be in pain: a disease or soreness of the eyes
<thu>, matter, with <muhzia>, way of seeing: how a person looks at and understands matters
the ethnic nationalities of Myanmar, the native peoples other than the Burman majority, as a group in national politics
<ngawng>, neck, with <khauh>, stiff: unwilling to yield or obey although one knows what is right
the ailment of a neck so stiff that the head cannot be turned; one article uses it as a picture of rigid thinking
split into two or more branches, as a tree, a horn, a tail or a line of thought; also the fork or branch itself
<i> and <kisam> written as one word: we need, it is necessary for us
<bawm>, basket, with <pua>, carry on the back: one who carries a basket on the back; an article gives it as the meaning of the name Chin
<gankhawi> with the noun suffix {-na}: the keeping and rearing of animals, or the place where they are kept, often named with <lokhawhna>, farming
<deuh> and <ta> written as one word after a describing word or verb: has now become somewhat more so
<huam> and <lo> written as one word: does not cover, does not include
{a ci} written as one word in the spelling of neighbouring dialects, with {chi} for <ci>: he or she says, they call it
plural of <Zolia>: the young unmarried women of the Zomi
<gelh>, write, with <pih>, do together with or for someone: write something for or with another person
placed after a verb: in a limp, drooping or half-hearted way, without strength or firmness
<galte>, enemies, with the subject marker <in> shortened and written as one word: the enemies as the doers of the action
placed after a verb of shaking, sounding or speaking: with force and without stopping, as {ling kangkang}, tremble violently
<kipat> and <ding> written as one word: will begin, that is to be started
in songs and sayings, <sial.4>, mithun, and <bang.2>, like, written as one word: like a mithun, said of what grows great and strong
<lung>, heart or mind, with <puakzia>, way of carrying: the attitude of mind that a person or a people holds
<kilom>, in one mass, with <khawm>, together: come together and hold together as one group or people
<teel>, choose, with the ending {-pi}, great: a general election for parliament, also written <kiteelpi>
a city in the state of Haryana, India, next to Delhi
<pai> and <leng.1> written as one word: if I or we go, when one goes
the capital city of the state of Nagaland in northeast India
a traditional Zomi cloth for men, in former times worn by those honoured for bravery in war or hunting; usually {Tangcing puan}
<an>, food, with <tawi>, carry: cooked food carried as a gift to relatives by custom, as at a feast or for a newborn child in {nau antawi}
<khak.4>, send, and <thei>, can, written as one word: can send; with <ki> before it, can be sent
a Zomi village in the Tedim area of Chin State, Myanmar; {Simzang gam} is the tract around it
<meidet>, torch, with the noun suffix {-na}: the lighting and carrying of torches at the Khuado festival
